# Component model sources

The viewer retains the actual enclosure meshes and imports the two manufacturer models below. Other components use detailed visual models at the positions in `parameters.json`; they are not manufacturer-certified geometry or new fit measurements.

## Adafruit TLV320DAC3100

`6309.step` is the unmodified Adafruit TLV320DAC3100 board model downloaded on 2026-09-11 from [Adafruit_CAD_Parts](https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit_CAD_Parts/tree/main/6309%20TLV320DAC3100%20I2S%20DAC). Copyright Adafruit Industries; the repository's MIT license is included as `LICENSE-Adafruit-CAD.txt`. The assembly-coordinate derivative is generated by `build.py` and retains this attribution/license.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adafruit/Adafruit_CAD_Parts/main/6309%20TLV320DAC3100%20I2S%20DAC/6309%20TLV320DAC3100%20I2S%20DAC.step

Nominal imported bounds: X 0–33.5370095, Y 0–25.4, Z 0–6.372483 mm. PCB body: X 0–31.75, Y 0–25.4, Z 0–1.57 mm. Socket bore axis runs along X at Y 16.7591527, Z 3.872483 mm; socket mouth X 33.5370095 mm. These are extracted CAD values. The published product envelope is larger: 33.7 × 25.4 × 7.1 mm, and controls the enclosure allocation.

The repacked P04 transforms vendor coordinates as Xcase = Yvendor − 12.7, Ycase = Xvendor + 21.7, Zcase = 11.6 − Zvendor. This turns the socket toward the top and the component face toward the LCD. No component is removed or flattened. Both renderer and CAD derive the translation from the DAC position in `parameters.json`. The [orientation study](../studies/dac_orientation/README.md) also exports the opposite face as an explicitly non-manufacturing CAD reference.

`6309.brd`, if present in the working folder, was downloaded separately from [Adafruit's PCB repository](https://github.com/adafruit/Adafruit-TLV320DAC3100-I2S-DAC-PCB) for inspection only. It is not used by the build or redistributed in the deliverable ZIP; that repository has its own license.

The viewer reads the original STEP assembly, including colors on faces and nested solids. The brown mechanical substrate is rendered with a black solder mask matching [Adafruit's production board photographs](https://www.adafruit.com/product/6309). Silk labels are illustrative. Board, connectors, ICs, passives, holes and placement retain the source geometry.

## Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3

`XIAO-ESP32S3 v2.step` is the unmodified STEP from the [official XIAO ESP32-S3 model download](https://files.seeedstudio.com/wiki/SeeedStudio-XIAO-ESP32S3/res/seeed-studio-xiao-esp32s3-3d_model.zip), linked under Mechanical Design in [Seeed's documentation](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/#resources). Downloaded 2026-09-11; the STEP header identifies a 2023-05-27 export. Attribution: Seeed Studio. The archive includes no separate model license; [Seeed's publisher terms](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/License/) identify associated documents/images as CC BY-SA 4.0 and retain third-party rights. No MIT license is asserted for this model.

The viewer retains the board, castellations, USB-C shell and contacts, shield, buttons and U.FL socket. It adds illustrative shield text. It does not add the Sense camera board, fitted headers or an external antenna.

The STEP's PCB bounds are X -8.67334 to 12.28284, Y -0.25 to 1.0, Z -15.0014 to 2.7786 mm. It is rotated with its USB opening toward the right-hand case port: Xcase = Xvendor - 1.80475 + Xboard, Ycase = -Zvendor - 6.1114 + Yboard, Zcase = Yvendor + 0.25 + Zboard. Dimensions are not scaled. The USB body extends beyond the PCB and the nominal 4.2 mm planning depth. The compact build additionally checks this unscaled vendor geometry against both shells, other component envelopes and routing reserves; `validation.json` records that check separately from nominal envelope checks.

## Modeled visual references

| Part | Visible construction | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| ST7789 LCD | PCB with mounting holes/pads, metal backlight pan, black bezel, flex and separate screen surface | Existing 52 x 40 x 2.8 mm envelope; exact purchased board unidentified |
| 4th-gen clickwheel | Face and center button, support tabs, metal backing, tactile domes, sensor flex, controller and flex tail | Confirmed monochrome wheel family; assumed dimensions and representative underside |
| 503040 cell | Rounded foil pouch, sealed edges, protection tape, label, red/black leads and two-contact plug | Selected 40 x 30 x 5 mm / 600 mAh pack; finish and connector remain representative |
| microSD module | Drilled PCB, gold pads, open metal cage, spring contacts and inserted card edge | Existing 22 x 18 mm envelope; slot faces the actual right-side CAD opening |
| 8-pin FPC adapter | Drilled PCB, fan-out traces, 0.5 mm contacts, bottom-contact socket and locking latch | Existing 26.1 x 19.1 mm allocation and user-confirmed connector type; no upright headers |

The short flex tails and battery leads show component construction, not a validated wiring harness. The pouch, tape and label rotate together by 90 degrees in the compact layout. Browser verification exports the detailed models as assembly-coordinate STLs under `reference_only/`, omitting label/screen planes. These references are not printable hardware; `build.py` continues to own manufacturing solids and conservative fit envelopes.

The LCD UI is a texture on the display's 40.8 x 30.6 mm active area, just ahead of its Z=1.4 mm face. The separate 0.6 mm lens remains clear at Z=0.1 mm. The texture is depth-tested, follows the display's explosion offset and is hidden with the display, independently of the lens and bezel.

## Viewer libraries

Three.js 0.180.0 (MIT) and Lucide 0.468.0 (ISC) are bundled for offline use. Notices are in `LICENSE-viewer.txt` and embedded in `preview.html`. The JavaScript source is `../viewer.js`; `../package-lock.json` pins the build dependencies.
